summary: Keep‑alive connection reuse causes per-connection batch imbalance and intermittent p95/p99 spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes and occasional 504s for short streaming and unary requests. Spikes correlate with periods where a small number of long‑lived keep‑alive connections dominate traffic from the customer's SDK pool.

Impact:
- NimbusHealth observed p99 increasing from ~180ms baseline to ~1.8s during spikes (user‑facing latency for inference requests).
- ~0.4% increase in 504 timeouts during the window.
- Affects live clinical triage flows (low tolerance for tail latency).

Environment:
- Customer tier: dedicated
- Region: prod us-east-1
- SDK: redwood-js v1.6.2 with default http keepalive settings
- Workload: many long‑lived streaming connections reused for frequent short prompts (5–20 tokens)

Steps to reproduce (customer repro):
1) Start 200 client processes that establish persistent keep‑alive connections to the Redwood endpoint.
2) Each client reuses its connection and sends short generation requests at 1–5 QPS per connection.
3) Observe p95/p99 in Grafana and increase in the batch coalescer per-connection queue depth.

Observed behavior:
- Continuous coalescer queues become imbalanced: a few connections accumulate longer queues and larger microbatches while most remain nearly empty.
- When those overloaded connections flush, head‑of‑line latency increases for requests sharing the same worker leading to p95/p99 spikes and occasional downstream timeouts.
- Trace snippets show long wait time in "coalescer.enqueue" before entering batch worker.

Expected behavior:
- Even distribution of requests into microbatches so no single connection causes persistent head‑of‑line blocking.

Logs / dashboards referenced:
- https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abcd/continuous-batcher?from=now-2h&to=now (high queue depth by connection)
- https://sentry.redwood.com/issue/INV-6612 (sample traces showing enqueue wait)
- Customer-provided pcap and SDK logs attached in ticket attachments.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 12:05 UTC — Initial triage by Support: correlated customer p99 spikes with coalescer queueing metrics. Noted that spikes aligned to periods after client pool warm-up.
2026-03-10 15:40 UTC — SRE attached coalescer debug dump: per-connection queue counters show top 5 connections holding ~70% of pending messages during spike windows.
2026-03-11 09:10 UTC — Hypothesis: linger/flush timer state is tracked per TCP connection and is not reset correctly on connection reuse, producing imbalanced linger windows and sticky microbatches.
2026-03-11 11:30 UTC — Ran synthetic experiment: recreated workload with controlled keepalive reuse and observed same skew. When clients used short‑lived connections, p99 returned to baseline.

2026-03-11 16:50 UTC — Reviewed redwood-js SDK v1.6.2 connection pooling code; found aggressive connection reuse combined with exponential backoff on failed flushes can produce persistent per-connection queueing.

2026-03-12 08:20 UTC — Confirmed interaction between API gateway connection affinity and worker assignment: gateway tends to reuse same backend connection for clients behind NAT which amplifies per‑connection skew for high fan‑out customers.

2026-03-12 10:00 UTC — Root cause narrowed to two interacting factors: (1) per-connection linger timer + queue bookkeeping that biases selection, and (2) gateway affinity causing uneven mapping of client connections to worker processes.
comments: Support (Aisha Nayar) 2026-03-10 12:20 UTC: Reached out to NimbusHealth. Asked for SDK logs, approximate spike windows, and whether they use connection pooling or serverless frontends. Customer responded with sample load generator and timestamps.
SRE (Ben Castillo) 2026-03-10 15:55 UTC: Ran quick coalescer dump; seeing per-connection queue hot spots. Scheduling deeper instrumented run tomorrow. Linking SUP-9371 for similar symptoms in past.

Customer (Nina Patel, NimbusHealth) 2026-03-11 08:40 UTC: Confirmed that switching SDK to 'forceNewConnection' mitigates the spike. Happy to test recommended workarounds while you investigate permanent fix.

Dev (Ravi Mehta) 2026-03-11 14:05 UTC: Found that linger state is stored in connection metadata and not cleared on reuse. Drafting PR to clear linger/timestamp on checkout. Also evaluating a global per-worker aggregator as alternate approach.

Support (Aisha Nayar) 2026-03-12 09:45 UTC: Shared temporary mitigation steps with customer: (1) set SDK env var REDWOOD_CONNECTION_REUSE=false, (2) reduce keepalive lifetime to 30s, (3) scale gateway pool to reduce affinity. Customer will test this afternoon.
SRE (Ben Castillo) 2026-03-12 12:30 UTC: Instrumentation shows p99 back to ~210ms in controlled test with reduced keepalive; good sign. Planning staged deploy of fix in dev cluster next week.
Customer (Nina Patel) 2026-03-12 17:10 UTC: Mitigation helped significantly in our staging environment. Please let us know planned timeline for permanent fix since production depends on it.
root_cause: Per-connection linger/queue bookkeeping in the continuous coalescer combined with API gateway connection affinity caused persistent microbatch imbalance. Long‑lived keep‑alive connections accumulated queued requests and created head‑of‑line blocking when flushed, producing p95/p99 spikes and intermittent timeouts.
resolution: Temporary workaround provided to customer: disable aggressive connection reuse in SDK (REDWOOD_CONNECTION_REUSE=false) or shorten keepalive TTL; scale gateway frontends to reduce single‑connection affinity. Engineering drafted a fix to clear linger state on connection checkout and added a fallback to global aggregation when per-connection queue imbalance crosses threshold. Patch PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2891. Plan: deploy to staging 2026-03-18, canary to low‑traffic dedicated clusters 2026-03-20, full rollout 2026-03-25 pending monitoring.
